---
engine: markdown
title: "Delimited text (CSV/TSV)"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

CSV is the default format. Use `--delimiter` (`-d`) for other separators and
`--no-header` (`-H`) for files without a header row. For finer control, use
`--input-delimiter` and `--output-delimiter` (`-D`) to set them independently,
`--no-input-header` and `--no-output-header` to control headers per side,
or `-F`/`-O` to force a specific format regardless of extension.

## Reading CSV

```{term}
rush run 'df |> dplyr::filter(mpg > 25) |> dplyr::select(mpg, cyl, hp)' mtcars.csv
```

## Reading TSV

```{term}
rush convert -O tsv -o mtcars.tsv mtcars.csv
rush run 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.tsv
```

## Delimiter control

### `--delimiter` (`-d`)

Override the delimiter for both reading and writing:

```{term}
rush run -d "\t" 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv | cat
```

### `--input-delimiter`

Override only the input delimiter while keeping the output as CSV:

```{term}
rush run --input-delimiter "\t" 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.tsv
```

### `--output-delimiter` (`-D`)

Override only the output delimiter:

```{term}
rush run -D "|" 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv
```

### Independent input and output delimiters

Read tab-separated input, write semicolons:

```{term}
rush run --input-delimiter "\t" -D ";" 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.tsv
```

## Format flags

### `--input-format` (`-F`)

Force a specific input format regardless of extension:

```{term}
cp mtcars.csv mtcars.txt
rush run -F csv 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.txt
rm -f mtcars.txt
```

### `--output-format` (`-O`)

Force a specific output format:

```{term}
rush run -O tsv 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv
```

Write as tab-separated even when piping (no output file):

```{term}
rush run -O tsv 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv | cat
```

## Header control

### `--no-header` (`-H`)

Suppress the header on both input (no column names in the file) and output:

```{term}
echo -e "1,Alice\n2,Bob\n3,Carol" | rush run -H 'df'
```

### `--no-input-header`

Read a file without a header row, but still include a header in the output:

```{term}
echo -e "1,Alice\n2,Bob\n3,Carol" | rush run --no-input-header 'df'
```

### `--no-output-header`

Read normally but suppress the header in the output:

```{term}
rush run --no-output-header 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv | cat
```

### `--names`

Provide explicit column names (comma-separated). Implies `--no-input-header`:

```{term}
echo -e "1,Alice\n2,Bob\n3,Carol" | rush run --names "id,name" 'df'
```

## Limiting output with `--head`

Limit output to the first N rows:

```{term}
rush run --head 5 'df' mtcars.csv
```

Works with any output format:

```{term}
rush run --head 3 -O tsv 'df' mtcars.csv
```

Combined with SQL:

```{term}
rush sql --head 3 "SELECT * FROM mtcars ORDER BY mpg DESC" mtcars.csv
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.tsv
```
